references.text: The tribe of Judah also failed to drive out the Jebusites from Jerusalem, illustrating a similar pattern where the Israelites were unable to expel the Canaanites.
The tribe of Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, another parallel example of the tribes' inability to complete the conquest.
It repeats almost verbatim that Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of these cities and that the Canaanites continued to live in the land.
It explains that the tribes could not drive out the inhabitants of the valleys because they had iron chariots, providing context for why the Canaanites were allowed to remain.
The angel of the Lord rebukes Israel for failing to drive out the peoples and warns that these will become a snare to them.
God's original promise to gradually drive out the nations, which provides background for why the Canaanites were still in the land.
A warning that if the Israelites do not drive out the inhabitants of the land, they will become thorns in their eyes.
